## 🏛️ 1. **Architecture Timeline**  
*Focus: Vatican Palace projects, palace renovations, and architectural style evolution*

| Year | Event | Key Details |
|------|------|-----------|
| **1512–1542** | Early life in Naples; moves to Rome | Leaves Naples at age 20; enters art world after Polidoro da Caravaggio’s departure. Begins painting façades. |
| **1542** | First documented contract | Decorates loggia of Archbishop of Benevento; known for use of **grotesque style** (Raphael/Mannerist). |
| **1544–1553** | Fresco at Oratory of San Giovanni Decollato | Paints *The Dance of Salome*; reflects Raphaelesque and Mannerist style. One of few surviving large works. |
| **1558** | Hired as *Architetto Fabricae Palatinae* (Vatican Palace Architect) | Appointed by Pope Paul IV; works with assistant Sallustio Peruzzi. |
| **1556** | Chapel construction begins | Designed two large angel paintings for the new papal apartment; completed in ~10 months. |
| **1558–1560** | Hall of Constantine renovation | Replaced dark interior with **roof garden** to increase natural light. |
| **1558–1560** | Monstrance (tabernacle) commission | Begun for papal trips; unfinished when Paul IV dies; completed under Pius IV and sent to Milan. |
| **1560** | Casino of Pius IV begins | Revamped Paul IV’s original plan: includes **second story, large fountain, oval courtyard**. Named in honor of Pius IV. Called “the most beautiful afternoon retreat” by Jacob Burckhardt. |
| **1560** | Honorary Roman citizenship | Awarded to only three people: Michelangelo, Titian, Fra Guglielmo della Porta. Boosts commissions. |
| **1560–1565** | Nicchione renovation | Adds **semicircular loggia** at northern end of Belvedere Court; later used as fireworks site. |
| **1565** | Open-air theater built | Completed at southern end of Belvedere Court; torn down in 18th century. Designed to be viewed from pope’s window. |
| **1565** | Vatican Archives project | Designed a **modest, utilitarian archive**—a departure from his ornate style. Focused on function over decoration. |
| **1564** | Appointed architect of San Pietro Church | Annoys Giorgio Vasari; works with Giacomo Vignola; little progress; eventually dismissed. |
| **1565** | Brief imprisonment | Accused of stealing building materials; writings removed; medallions worth 6,000 scudi confiscated. |
| **1567** | Final years at Vatican | Works on minor projects; returns to Ferrara. Retains title until possibly June 1567. |

🔹 **Pattern Insight**:  
Ligorio’s architectural style evolved from **Raphaelesque/Mannerist** to **functional yet ornate**. His work under Pius IV emphasized **completion of unfinished projects**, reflecting a deep respect for classical order and continuity—mirroring his antiquarian values.
